messages:
sam_p: Quick post-all-hands note: thanks for the runtime roadmap clarity. A couple of teams asked for a compact list of who owns what for the batching/caching/kernel items and any short-lived mitigations folks can apply. Can we capture here?

maria_r: Agree. I'll summarize from the talk: first priority is the surprising p99 spikes on high-concurrency traffic. Short term: triage and hotfix if it's heuristic/config. Owner: maria_r + joel_s. ETA: 1 week.

kai_w: Tech note: spikes appear when our continuous batching combines a few long seq requests with many short ones. That causes KV cache misses and bigger latency variance. I can put up a small patch to separate batches by seq-length buckets and add a 8-12ms batching window cap. Prototype by EOD Friday.

jen_l: Model-side nuance: quant fallback sometimes forces a kernel that has hotter lock contention for certain attention ops. Medium term: build a kernel compatibility map and automatic ordering so we pick the fastest compatible kernel for given quant+seq_len. Owner: jen_l + eng-runtime. ETA: 3-4 weeks for MVP.

joel_s: Ops item: increase trace sampling for routes hitting model-alpha to 10-15% so we can correlate kernel choice + KV cache behavior. I'll open the tracing change PR and add the runbook link.

sam_p: Can we suggest a temporary workaround teams can opt into now?

maria_r: Yes: header workaround X-RW-Serve: low_latency will force split-by-length routing to the faster variant (falls back if capacity missing). We'll add Console docs and a short FAQ.

kai_w: Another quick tip: set prefer_cached: true for stable prompts and short seqs; that pushes traffic to cached prefix paths and often cuts 50-70ms for many flows.

jen_l: Also recommend using model-variant: vfast where available for latency-sensitive endpoints. Note this variant may have different token pricing. We'll list tradeoffs in the Console.

sam_p: Risk assessment for the batching cap?

maria_r: Risk: smaller batches -> more CPU per token and potentially higher cost. Mitigation: canary rollout + quick revert via FF. We'll run canary at 5% for 30m then 25% if stable.

kai_w: Pseudo-config we'll use:

```
batching:
  enabled: true
  window_ms: 10
  split_strategy: seq_len_buckets
  max_batch_tokens: 128000
```

This will be behind feature flag batching.window_ms.

joel_s: Notification process: open an incidents thread and tag @eng-sre. Also use Console -> Report latency issue shortcut, which creates the ticket and links to the runbook. I'll wire the shortcut to the new runbook today.

sam_p: Measurables? How will we know success?

maria_r: Short-term: reduce p99 regressions (p99 > 350ms incidents) on model-alpha from ~5/week to <=1/week. Medium-term: reduce p99 by 15-20% across the top-3 heavy models after kernel ordering + quant fixes.

kai_w: In lab tests separating seq_len buckets reduced tail by ~28% for mixed distributions. Production validation will confirm.

jen_l: Delivery milestones: kernel map MVP (top 10 models) + eval hooks in Console for post-rollout regen checks 18 days. Regression alerting tied to eval prompts after that.

sam_p: Can each owner drop a tiny public issue/PR link when they start so PLG teams can track?

maria_r: Will do. Creating GH project board and adding the actions now.

kai_w: ACTION: ship batching FF prototype (owner: kai_w) 1 days for canary prototype, 2 weeks for phased rollout.

maria_r: ACTION: triage p99 spikes + hotfix if heuristic (owner: maria_r + joel_s)  days.

jen_l: ACTION: kernel compatibility matrix + console eval hooks (owner: jen_l) 3-28 days.

joel_s: ACTION: increase trace sampling + runbook + Console shortcut (owner: joel_s)  days.

sam_p: I'll summarize in the all-hands follow-up doc and add to the roadmap section. Weekly check-ins; please update the GH board when you hit milestones. :thumbsup:

canary-bot: canary deploy 1901234900 started by kai_w % traffic  status: running

kai_w: quick note after 15m: canary p95 ~ stable, tail appears improved on the sampled routes. I'll post a short trace bundle in #eng-runtime after 30m. :eyes:
